findings.element: states.publish copy handler (render-b.js:1810-1827) against the dead copy branch in wireOwner (render-b.js:1270-1288); the owner bar's verb and the "Only you can see this" status line
findings.problem: Driven end to end on BOTH grounds with a stubbed clipboard: owner-empty, type "3 October 2026", Set the day, Add a moment, name it, Escape, Publish, Copy the link (the URL genuinely reaches the clipboard), Back to the plan. The plan still reads "Only you can see this", the primary verb is still "Publish", and pressing it again lands on "Send it to Aisling & Tom." Identical from state=owner-draft, on paper and on ink. The product's own model is written into the code -- "Taking the link IS the publish in this model, so the verb, the status line and the press heading flip once, together, at the moment it becomes someone else's" -- but that branch lives in wireOwner, which is only wired onto ownerSurface, and the owner surface carries no [data-act=copy] control. The only Copy the link button in the product is on states.publish, whose own handler sets "Copied" / "Link copied." and never touches F.publication. So no plan built through this product ever leaves draft: "Live since 15 July - anyone with the link can read it", the "Get the link" verb and "Mara & Finn have had this since 15 July." are reachable only because the demonstration fixture is pre-seeded as published. The one question the owner of a wedding actually asks this screen -- have they got it yet -- is answered "Only you can see this" forever, and the reassurance "You can turn the link off at any time" promises an on/off state the product never enters. This is not round 8's publish-contradicts-its-own-headline (a published plan offering "Publish"); it is the inverse, and round 9's draft-branch-restored-before-it-is-used drove this exact path but stopped one press short of Copy.
findings.fix: Extract the flip into one function used by both handlers: takeTheLink() { if (F.publication.state !== "published") { F.publication = { state: "published", publishedAt: F.today }; F.updatedLabel = F.fmt.medium(F.today) + " " + F.fmt.year(F.today); } }. Call it from the success path of states.publish's writeText, then rewrite the press heading from the same accessor that built it (F.publication.state === "published" ? name + " have had this since " + F.fmt.medium(F.publication.publishedAt) + "." : "Send it to " + name + ".") so the screen the owner is standing on changes under them, and let paintPublication pick the rest up when go("owner-flight") remounts. Delete the now-duplicated dead branch in wireOwner. A correction, not an architectural change: about twenty lines, no new state and no new string.

findings.element: the undo bar (.b-undo) across the Preview and Get the link round trips; history.length = 0 in render (render-b.js:2034)
findings.problem: The owner's most ordinary loop is: change something, look at it as a guest, come back. Driven at 1440 on both grounds -- open Menu tasting at The Orchard, press Hidden, press Done: the bar reads "Menu tasting at The Orchard is now hidden from guests." with Undo live and data-undo set. Press Preview, then Back to the plan: the moment is still hidden, the bar is empty, .b-undoAct is disabled, data-undo is gone, and Ctrl+Z does nothing. The plan survives the round trip (the gate asserts that) but the reversal does not, and nothing on screen says it was spent. The Publish round trip does the same. So checking your work is the act that makes it permanent -- the class the defect library names by name (never destroy the control that would undo it). The cause is real rather than cosmetic: every undo entry closes over live DOM nodes (item, node, measureEl), so the stack cannot simply be kept across a remount without pointing at detached elements.
findings.fix: This is a BUILD, not a mid-round correction -- put it on the founder's list. Make undo entries re-resolvable rather than node-bound: entries already carry entry.id, so replace the captured element references with lookups against the live DOM at undo time (root.querySelector('.b-item[data-id=' + id + ']')) and record each reversal as data -- previous ISO date, previous title, previous visibility, previous index -- instead of as a closure over the node. Then scope history.length = 0 to a genuinely fresh load rather than to every render, and have go() call paintUndo(root) after C.mount() so the bar redraws whatever is still on the stack. Roughly half a day, confined to remember / undo / paintUndo and the four call sites in wireOwner.

findings.element: .b-live on the owner-empty first-add path (render-b.js:1627 go("owner-flight"), string at render-b.js:1432)
findings.problem: On a brand-new project -- the one path where the owner has never seen a plan at all -- pressing Add a moment routes through go("owner-flight"), which writes the fixed string "Back to the plan." into the live region. Measured after Set the day then Add a moment on state=owner-empty at 390 and at 1440, on both grounds: document.querySelector('.b-live').textContent === "Back to the plan." The owner is not going back to anything; they have just made the first moment of their first plan, and the only thing spoken to them at that transition is false. It is also inconsistent with the same button on a seeded plan, which correctly announces "A moment was added." through remember(). SAID is keyed by destination state, so every arrival at owner-flight says the same sentence whatever it came from.
findings.fix: Key the announcement to the transition rather than the destination. In the owner-empty add handler, after go("owner-flight") and before openEditor, overwrite it: var live = document.querySelector(".b-live"); if (live) live.textContent = "A moment was added." -- the string this same action already uses on a seeded plan. Two lines.

findings.element: the hairline above "Today is 16 July" in states.loading and states.loading-slow (render-b.js:1962) against .b-todayRule on the arrived surface (b.css:101)
findings.problem: Measured at 390 on both grounds, loading against phone: the rule sits at exactly y=271 in both frames and the label under it at y=280 in both -- the geometry is right, and the four skeleton bars match the real objects they stand for to within 2px. But the loading frame hand-rolls this one element as a plain div at background: var(--fore-16), width 350, while the arrived surface renders .b-todayRule at background: var(--accent), width 344. So at the moment the plan lands, the single accent mark on the received screen changes hue -- grey to indigo -- and shortens by 6px. Nothing about that rule was ever pending: the label directly beneath it is printed as real text in the loading frame, because today is known before the data is. The state's own comment says the frame draws only what is known and reserves it at its real geometry; this is the one object where it draws a known thing in the pending token. Identical on paper and on ink.
findings.fix: Replace h("div", { style: "height:1px;background:var(--fore-16);margin:26px 0 0" }) in states.loading with h("div.b-todayRule", { style: "margin:26px 0 0" }), so the rule is the same object, the same token and the same 344px in both frames. One line; loading-slow inherits it.

biggestWin: The measure is the product, and it holds up under driving. At 390, 700, 768, 1152, 1279, 1280 and 1440 on both grounds, the vertical distance between two rows IS the number of days between them -- the 320px of deliberate nothing between "Today, 16 July" and the first moment is the fourteen empty days, and the stacked 8 August pair I made by pressing +7 twice collapsed onto one mark with one count rather than overprinting. Nothing has to explain it: the numeral column states the distance, the mono line states the date, the one filled indigo tick states which is next, and the indigo rail states how much is still ahead. One idea carried without a second colour, a second weight or a legend. It survives being operated: setAway is the only writer of a distance, so the count, the date, the accessible name and the stepper readout moved together on every move I made, and the undo stack popped them back in the right order with the scroll position intact. The empty project deserves its own mention -- three distinct refusals for three distinct wrong answers, the question removed from the screen the instant it is answered, and today stated on the second screen a new owner ever sees.
